items.evidence: tests/npcSlice3b.test.ts:57-60 (and 3a:63-66) `const seq = (...vals: number[]): Rng => { let i = 0; return () => vals[Math.min(i++, vals.length - 1)] ?? 0; };`
items.detail:
`Math.min(i++, vals.length - 1)` pins the index at the last element once `i` passes it, so `seq(0.9)` hands 0.9 to call 1, call 2, call 3 … indefinitely. `?? 0` only fires for `seq()` with no args (`vals.length - 1` is -1, `vals[-1]` is undefined) → a no-arg seq returns 0 forever. `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true` in tsconfig is why the `?? 0` is there at all.
IMPLICATION the parent needs: the clamp is precisely what let `seq(0.9)` silently feed the same value to two rolls with different bands, and it is why a seq can never signal "you under-sized me". rollsFor must therefore be the signal. A rollsFor that reports only a COUNT is enough to make the fix writable (`seq(0.9, 0.9, 0.5)`), but it does not by itself name the failing band — see the A3 item.

PARKING BY DIRECT ASSIGNMENT (used deliberately to bypass the clip/roll side effects): tests/npcSlice3b.test.ts:206 `b.actionState = OG_STATE.FALL; // FALL is in the list`; :284 `a.actionState = OG_STATE.FLY;`; :140 `dying.actionState = OG_STATE.DYING;`; :652 `a.actionState = OG_STATE.GOTLAUNCHED;`. items.claim: Failure (1) is NEITHER parked() nor rollsFor(). Nothing left a state and no rng was rolled. A third check is required: the body MUTATED a counter the test wrote in setup BEFORE the body READ it.

items.detail:
WHY NOT parked(): the bear was parked in RUN and, in the failing version, left RUN for ATTACK — but leaving RUN is exactly the BEHAVIOUR UNDER TEST elsewhere in the same file (tests/npcSlice3a.test.ts:318-337 asserts RUN → ATTACK at 99 px). A parked(a, RUN) assertion would have produced a nicer message ("RUN → ATTACK") than `expected 10 to be 1`, but it is the same claim restated, not a preflight: it cannot fire before the assertion it duplicates, and it would be WRONG in the neighbouring test. It also cannot distinguish "the actor moved because the test mis-set a counter" from "the actor moved because that is the port's behaviour".
WHY NOT rollsFor(): the RUN branch reaching the swing makes ZERO rng calls — `startAction(OG_STATE.ATTACK)` (src/core/npc/EnemyBear.ts:144-150) only faces and starts a clip. No seq is involved; rollsFor would return 0 either way.
WHAT A THIRD CHECK MUST DO — report the value the branch ACTUALLY READ, versus the value setup WROTE. Two implementable shapes:
  (a) RUNTIME, mechanical: an access tracer. `useDefineForClassFields: true` makes `idleCounter` an own, configurable property on the instance (src/core/npc/EnemyBear.ts:44 `idleCounter = ZERO;`), so `Object.defineProperty(npc, 'idleCounter', { get, set, configurable: true })` can record the ORDER of reads and writes across a body. The preflight rule is: "the first touch of a field the test just wrote must be a READ, not a WRITE." One-line failure: `idleCounter: setup wrote 1, doAction() WROTE 0 before its first read — the value under test is spent this frame`. Suggested name alongside parked/rollsFor: `firstTouch(npc, field, fn)` or `tickOrder(npc, field, fn)`.
  (b) AUTHORING RULE, no instrumentation: any test that writes a threshold/counter field and asserts one side of the branch must assert BOTH sides. That is literally what the re-authored test is — the `swing(cooldown)` closure asserting 2 → RUN and 1 → ATTACK. This is what actually fixed it, and it generalises to the whole slice; it just cannot be enforced by a runtime helper.
HONEST CONCLUSION FOR THE PARENT: HARNESS_KICKOFF.md:133-134's claim that all three failures "shared one root: the test parked an actor in a state whose own doAction left it before the assertion ran" does NOT hold for this one. If T5 ships only parked() + rollsFor(), its own DONE criterion ("all three of session 35's failures are reproducible as one-line preflight failures") cannot be met — a third helper, or an amended criterion, is needed.

items.claim: Failure (2) IS parked() — with one design constraint the spec's wording hides: at SETUP time the alpha really is in FALL, so parked() only catches it if it is asserted AFTER the frames are driven (or if it also checks the state's own exit condition).
items.evidence: src/core/npc/EnemyWolfAlpha.ts:366-373 (the FALL case: `if (this.y >= this.world.groundY) { this.y = this.world.groundY; this.startAction(OG_STATE.LAND); }`) vs tests/npcSlice3b.test.ts:100 `npc.setPosition(400, GROUND);` inside `stats()`
items.detail:
SEQUENCE: `startAction(OG_STATE.FALL)` (EnemyWolfAlpha.ts:259-261) only calls `startAnim(WOLF_LAUNCHED)` — the actor IS in FALL when setup ends. The mover is the FIRST `update()`, whose `doAction()` FALL case finds `y (358) >= groundY (358)` with velY = 0 and calls `startAction(OG_STATE.LAND)`, which calls `startAnim(OG_ANIM.WOLF_LAUNCHEDEND)`.
SO: `parked(a, OG_STATE.FALL)` placed immediately after setup PASSES and catches nothing. Placed just before the assertion under test (after `for (let i = 0; i < CLIP; i++) a.update();`) it fails with exactly the right sentence: `FALL → LAND` / "the alpha left FALL for LAND". Two viable API shapes:
  (i) `parked(npc, state)` used as a post-drive assertion — simplest, and it needs the OG_STATE reverse lookup from item S1.
  (ii) `const still = parked(npc, state)` returning a re-checkable closure that captured the entry state, so the test reads `still()` after the drive — closer to the spec's "naming what moved it" (the closure can also report the anim, which is what actually masked the test: WOLF_LAUNCHEDEND replacing WOLF_POUNCE_MID).
A STRONGER (state-aware) version worth considering, since it fires BEFORE any frame: for FALL specifically the exit condition is knowable at setup — `y >= world.groundY` means FALL self-terminates on frame 1. A parked() that additionally asserts the parked state's own guard is not already satisfied would have caught this at the setup line, which is a genuine preflight rather than a better error message. Same pattern exists for GOTLAUNCHED (`doLaunched`, EnemyWolfAlpha.ts:446-461, lands to DOWNED when `y >= groundY`) and for the base Npc — so the check generalises across the whole npc suite family.
NOTE for the DONE-criterion demo: both halves of this test (alpha and wolf) share the trap, so removing either `setPosition(400, GROUND - 200)` line reproduces the failure.

items.claim: Failure (3) is rollsFor() only INDIRECTLY. The seq was mis-sized (1 value for 3 rolls), which is a count problem — but the count alone does not name the defect; the value 0.9 satisfying roll A's band and failing roll B's does. A count-only rollsFor turns an unreadable failure into a discoverable one, no more.
items.evidence: src/core/npc/EnemyWolfAlpha.ts:205 (howl: `asInt(this.rng() * OG_ALPHA.howlDice) === ZERO`) and :332 (walk: `asInt(this.rng() * OG_ALPHA.idle.walkDice) < OG_ALPHA.idle.walkBelow`), with src/config/ogEnemyWolfAlpha.ts:43 `howlDice: 3,` and :46 `idle: { snarlFrames: 24, retryFrames: 12, walkDice: 3, walkBelow: 2 },`
items.detail:
ROLL LEDGER for the cutscene test, derived by reading the call path (NOT executed — read-only mandate; the parent should confirm with `counting()`):
  #1 — inside `alpha()`'s constructor: EnemyWolfAlpha.ts:76 `this.startAction(OG_STATE.IDLE)` → the howl roll (:205).
  #2 — the test's own `a.startAction(OG_STATE.IDLE)` → the howl roll again (:205).
  #3 — `a.doAction()` IDLE case (:328-333): `idleCounter -= 1` → 0 → `<= 0` → retryFrames, faceTarget, then the WALK roll (:332). THIS is the roll 0.9 failed.
  #4, #5 — only if #3 passes: `startAction(OG_STATE.WALK)` rolls `destX` (:214) and then `walkSpeed` (:217 or :219).
So the body makes 3 rolls up to the decision and 5 across the whole test with 0.5; with 0.9 it makes 3 and stops in IDLE.
WHAT rollsFor BUYS: knowing "3 rolls before the decision" makes the fix writable as `seq(0.9, 0.9, 0.5)` — separate values per roll — instead of relying on the clamp (item R2) to feed one value to all three. That is exactly the mis-sizing the spec targets, so rollsFor is the right helper to CLAIM this failure.
WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY: the count is identical for 0.5 and 0.9 up to roll #3, so a count-only assertion is green in both worlds — it cannot fail as a preflight for THIS bug. To meet T5's "one-line preflight failure with a readable message" for failure (3), rollsFor should return the CONSUMED VALUES as well as the count (the `counting` helper already holds the shape: a callable with a mutable property), so a test can assert `rollsFor(...)` = `{ calls: 3, values: [0.9, 0.9, 0.9] }` and a preflight can say `seq has 1 value but this body rolls 3 — roll 3 (walkDice 3, needs < 2) got 0.9 → 2`. Also note the INVERSION: the alpha stayed in IDLE, i.e. it did NOT leave its setup state — the exact opposite of parked(), so parked() is useless here and would have been GREEN.

Scored against the source: (1) bear cooldown — the actor's state change was the ASSERTION, not an unwanted side effect; the root is write-then-tick ordering on `idleCounter` (see A1). (2) alpha FALL — TRUE, this is the stated root exactly. (3) rng 0.9 — the actor FAILED to leave IDLE; a "left its state" check is green. So the shared root is 1 of 3, not 3 of 3.
The same doc repeats the claim twice more — :42 (the evidence table row) and :243-244 ("all three shared one root — an actor parked in a state its own doAction left at once") — so a correction touches three places if the parent chooses to fix the doc in the same commit.
